Here they are. (It's only 2 PM on my end, but it sounds like you've had a long day, so skim now and come back to it.)

**Budget table, finished:**

| Item | Estimate | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Contingency fund | 10-15% of total | Covers surprises like fuel spikes, extra nights, and vet visits |

**Ballpark totals (1-2 bedroom, one dog, one car driven):**
- **DIY truck:** ~$4,000-$7,500 including truck, fuel, supplies, and lodging
- **Hybrid or container:** ~$5,000-$9,000
- **Full-service movers:** ~$7,500-$14,000+
- Add ~$900-$1,800 if you ship a second vehicle.

---

## PACKING: ROOM BY ROOM

**Timeline:** Start with storage, garage, and decor 5-6 weeks out. Do guest rooms and books 3-4 weeks out, kitchen and bedrooms the last week, and bathrooms and essentials the final 2 days.

- **Garage/storage:** Pack tools and hazardous items separately. Movers won't take propane, paint, or chemicals, so dispose of them properly.
- **Living room:** Wrap electronics in original boxes or blankets, and photograph cable setups before unplugging.
- **Kitchen (about 6 hrs):** Pack rarely used items first. Use dish packs for plates and stand them on edge. Keep 1 pan, 2 plates, utensils, and a kettle out.
- **Bedrooms:** Keep a bag of bedding and 3 days of clothes. Use wardrobe boxes or leave hanging clothes on hangers in bags.
- **Bathrooms:** Seal liquids in zip bags. Keep a toiletry kit and towels with you.
- **Office:** Back up computers, and carry laptops, hard drives, and documents yourself.
- **Dog items:** Keep the bed, bowls, food, and toys with you, not on the truck.

**Label every box** with room and contents, and number them. Mark "OPEN FIRST" boxes.

**Declutter tips:**
- Apply the "would I pay to move this?" test. Long-distance moves often cost $0.50-$1+ per pound.
- Sell bulky, cheap-to-replace furniture, since IKEA-type items often cost more to move than to replace.
- Do one category per weekend: clothes, books, kitchen, then miscellaneous.
- Donate with pickup services, and keep receipts for a possible tax deduction.
- Set a firm cutoff date for selling, and donate whatever is left.

---

## CANCEL AND START SERVICES

| When | Task | Who |
|---|---|---|
| 6-8 wks out | Schedule Oregon internet install; research providers | J |
| 4 wks | Notify employer, banks, insurers; start address-change list | J |
| 3 wks | Set Ohio utility shutoff for the day after you leave; schedule Oregon electric/gas/water start | J |
| 2 wks | Activate USPS forwarding; update subscriptions and Amazon | J |
| 2 wks | Pause or transfer gym, streaming, and meal kits; ask about transfer deals | P |
| 1 wk | Confirm all start and stop dates | M |
| Move day | Final meter photos | J |
| Week 1 after | Renter's or home insurance, auto insurance, and DMV updates | J |
| Week 2-4 after | Update remaining accounts, voter registration, and doctors | J |

---

## 8-WEEK REMINDER CALENDAR

**Assumed moving day: Thursday, July 16, 2026.** Shift all dates if yours differs. Note that July 4 weekend can affect truck, shipping, and utility availability.

- **May 21 (Wk -8):** Book movers or truck, and book vehicle shipping. Peak summer season fills up.
- **May 28 (Wk -7):** Sign the Oregon lease or confirm closing. Schedule internet.
- **Jun 4 (Wk -6):** Vet visit and records. Book lodging for the drive.
- **Jun 11 (Wk -5):** Start decluttering. Order boxes. Send landlord notice if not already sent.
- **Jun 18 (Wk -4):** Car maintenance. Review insurance. Notify employer if not done.
- **Jun 25 (Wk -3):** Schedule utilities. Begin packing non-essentials. Sell or donate large items.
- **Jul 2 (Wk -2):** Confirm movers and shipper (holiday week). Get the dog ID tag. Activate USPS forwarding.
- **Jul 9 (Wk -1):** Finish packing. Clean. Confirm everything. Pack the car and dog kit.
- **Jul 16:** Moving day.
- **Jul 17-31:** DMV, vet, dog license, insurance, address updates.

---

# PRINTABLE: MOVING DAY ESSENTIALS (keep in the car)

**DOCUMENTS (in one folder)**

**MONEY AND TECH**

- [ ] Phone chargers, car chargers, power bank

**DOG**

- [ ] Rabies certificate and vet records
- [ ] Medications and calming aids

**FIRST-NIGHT BAG (each person)**

**CAR AND SAFETY**
- [ ] Jumper cables, spare tire, and jack checked
- [ ] First aid kit, flashlight, and blanket
- [ ] Basic tools and tape
- [ ] Cleaning wipes and trash bags

**FINAL WALK-THROUGH**
- [ ] Photos or video of every room
- [ ] Lights, thermostat, and windows set

Two things first. My last two replies came through blank on my end, so the itinerary and cost comparison never reached you. And we already built a phased master checklist in my first reply, so tell me what you want from a new one (options at the bottom). Here is what's outstanding.

## Driving itinerary: Columbus to Portland (~2,490 mi, ~36-37 hrs of driving)

**Reality check:** True 3-day driving would be ~12.5 hrs a day, which is rough with a dog. This plan has 3 long days plus a short arrival day (Jul 17-20), matching your calendar. I-80 and I-84 is the flattest practical route, but it still crosses ~8,640 ft at Sherman Summit in Wyoming. It's a wide interstate and fine in July, but there's no truly low-elevation route. Times are estimates, so confirm in Google Maps or Waze.

| Day | Route | Drive time | Overnight |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Fri 7/17** | Columbus → Indianapolis → Champaign → Quad Cities → Des Moines | ~640 mi, 9.5-10 hrs (12 with stops) | Des Moines / West Des Moines, IA |
| **Sat 7/18** | Des Moines → Omaha → Lincoln → Kearney → North Platte → Cheyenne | ~640 mi, 9.5-10 hrs | Cheyenne, WY (see warning below) |
| **Sun 7/19** | Cheyenne → Laramie → Rock Springs → Evanston → Ogden → Twin Falls → Boise | ~780 mi, 11.5 hrs (13+ with stops) | Boise, ID |
| **Mon 7/20** | Boise → Baker City → La Grande → Pendleton → The Dalles → Portland | ~430 mi, 6.5-7 hrs | Arrive in Portland |

**Cheyenne warning:** Cheyenne Frontier Days normally runs for about 10 days in late July, and 2026 looks like it starts around Jul 17. Hotels may be sold out or expensive on Jul 18. Check dates now. Fallbacks are Laramie or Rawlins, or stopping short in North Platte, NE, and making up time later. If you change the overnight, edit the Day 2 and Day 3 calendar events.

**Dog stops (every 2-3 hrs):**
- **Day 1:** Use the pet areas at I-70/I-74 rest areas around Indianapolis and Champaign. Walk along the Mississippi riverfront at Davenport/LeClaire, and verify leash rules.
- **Day 2:** Stop at the Fort Kearny State Recreation Area or the Kearney Archway grounds (no dogs inside), and at North Platte rest areas.
- **Day 3:** Walk along the Snake River canyon rim in Twin Falls. In Boise, the Boise River Greenbelt is very dog-friendly, a good evening walk.
- **Day 4:** Stop at Hood River Waterfront Park or Cascade Locks Marine Park. Skip crowded Multnomah Falls with a dog.

**Lodging:** Chains like La Quinta, Red Roof Inn, and Motel 6 are typically pet-friendly, but confirm pet fees, weight limits, and ground-floor rooms in writing. Book now, since summer fills up.

**July safety:**
- The Snake River Plain and Columbia Gorge can top 95-100°F, so never leave the dog in the car.
- Walk early and late, and check pavement heat with your hand.
- Check wildfire smoke and road closures (fire.airnow.gov, 511 sites).

**Correction to the .ics:** The Day 2 event says you lose an hour. Going west you **gain** an hour, because clocks go back. Change that line to "Time zone change (gain 1 hr)". Also note Oregon's Ontario area switches to Pacific time.

## DIY truck vs hybrid vs full-service

Estimates for 1-2 bedrooms, one dog, and your own car driven. Get live quotes.

| | **DIY truck** | **Hybrid (container or labor-only)** | **Full-service movers** |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Total cost** | ~$4,000-7,500 | ~$5,000-9,000 | ~$7,500-14,000+ |
| **Your effort** | Highest: pack, load, drive, unload | Medium: pack and sometimes load or unload | Lowest |
| **Driving** | Two drivers, two vehicles (truck and car) | Just your car | Just your car |
| **Dog** | Dog rides in the car, so you need a second driver | Easiest | Easiest |
| **Timing risk** | Truck is slower, so add buffer. Book early, since July is peak | Containers can take 1-2+ weeks to deliver | Delivery is often 1-3 weeks after pickup, so you may arrive before your stuff |
| **Damage risk and coverage** | You carry the risk. Insurance is optional | Moderate. Check container coverage | Best with Full Value Protection ($200-500) |

**How to choose:**
- If you have a tight budget, a small load, and can both drive, go with the DIY truck.
- If you want to avoid driving a truck but keep costs down, go hybrid.
- If your time or physical capacity is limited, or you have a lot of furniture, go full-service.

Whichever you pick, plan for **temporary housing** and a **first-week kit**, since your belongings may arrive after you do.

## About the master checklist

Which of these would you like?
1. **One consolidated checklist** in a single list, merging the phased checklist, documents, and itinerary tasks.
2. **A checklist updated to your chosen path** (DIY, hybrid, or full-service), with irrelevant tasks removed.
3. **A tracker format** for Notion, Google Sheets, or a printable version, with who, due date, and status columns.

Tell me which one, and whether you've picked a moving method yet.

## CONTAINER DEPOSITS AND PAYMENT SCHEDULE

Terms vary by company, so confirm each one in writing.

| When | What | Typical amount |
|---|---|---|
| Booking (~May 21-28) | Reservation deposit, sometimes just a card hold | $0-$500 or ~10-25% |
| ~2 weeks before delivery | Remaining balance, if the company requires it up front | Varies |
| Delivery day | Fuel or delivery fees, extra-day charges | $0-$200 |
| After loading | Balance due on pickup (some companies bill on pickup) | Balance |
| Portland delivery | Storage or extra-day charges if you can't take delivery | $5-$25+/day |
| Local movers (load) | Deposit to hold the date | $0-$150 or 10-25% |
| Local movers (unload) | Same as above | $0-$150 or 10-25% |
| Day of service | Payment on completion, plus tips | Hourly total + tips |

Ask about **cancellation and rescheduling fees**, how many **free loading and unloading days** you get, and what **storage** costs if you arrive before your place is ready.

## PACKING BY ROOM: KEEP VS SELL

**Rule of thumb:** long-distance containers cost roughly $0.60-$1.50 per cubic foot of space. If an item costs less to replace than to ship, sell it.

| Room | Keep and ship | Sell or donate | Carry with you (not in container) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Living room** | Good sofa, TV, quality shelves, art | Worn furniture, cheap entertainment centers, old cables | Laptops, remotes, router |
| **Kitchen** | Daily dishes, good cookware, knives, small appliances you use weekly | Duplicates, chipped items, rarely used gadgets, half-used pantry | 1 pan, 2 plates, utensils, kettle for the first few days |
| **Bedrooms** | Mattress (bagged), dressers worth keeping, seasonal clothes | Particle-board furniture, worn bedding, outgrown clothes | 3-5 days of clothes, bedding bag, toiletries |
| **Bathrooms** | Towels, good shower items | Expired products, half-empty bottles | Toiletry kit and medications |
| **Office** | Desk if sturdy, monitors, files you need | Old cords, unused electronics, old paperwork (shred) | Laptops, hard drives, passports and documents |
| **Garage** | Quality tools, bikes, camping gear | Paint, chemicals, propane, clutter | Basic tool kit for the car |
| **Dog** | Large crate if you won't use it in the car, extra toys | Worn bedding and old toys | Bed, bowls, food, leash, meds, records, 3+ days of supplies |
| **Decor and misc.** | Sentimental items, photos | Anything you haven't used in a year | Valuables and jewelry |

**Container loading tips:** Disassemble beds and tables. Wrap furniture in blankets. Heavy boxes go low, light ones high. Leave no gaps. Don't pack liquids, hazmat, perishables, plants, firearms, or ammunition. Label with room and contents, and keep a numbered inventory.

## BALLPARK COSTS: CONTAINER HYBRID (Columbus to Portland)

| Option | Typical total | What's included |
|---|---|---|
| **U-Pack-style freight container, you load and unload** | ~$2,500-$5,000 | Delivery, pickup, transport, some loading time. Often the cheapest |
| **PODS-style container, you load and unload** | ~$3,500-$6,500 | Delivery, pickup, transport, a storage period |
| **Add local load and unload crews (2 movers, 3-4 hrs each end)** | +$600-$1,600 | ~$150-$250 per hour for 2 movers |
| **Add labor-only help from an online marketplace** | +$300-$900 | Cheaper but variable quality, so read reviews |
| **Full container + crews total** | ~$3,500-$8,000 | |
| **Packing supplies** | $150-$400 | |
| **Extra coverage** | $100-$400 | |

**Rest of the trip (any option):**

| Item | Estimate |
|---|---|
| Fuel for the car, ~2,490 mi | $250-$450 |
| Lodging, 3-4 nights with pet fees | $450-$900 |
| Meals and tolls | $250-$450 |
| Temporary housing, 1-2 weeks | $800-$2,000 |
| Oregon DMV, utility deposits, dog license | $250-$700 |
| Contingency, 10-15% | ~$500-$1,200 |

**Overall:** about **$6,000-$12,000** all-in for a 1-2 bedroom container hybrid. With a small load and careful sales, you can land near the low end. A bigger load with hired crews on both ends pushes toward the top.

**Container vs. local movers:** Containers typically win on price and flexibility, because you pack on your own timeline. Local crews add cost but save your backs, and they're worth it for heavy items, stairs, or tight timing.
